entries.title: Vault is sealed
entries.summary: The node is sealed: the barrier key is not in memory, so every request except status/unseal is rejected with HTTP 503.
internal_causes: Node was restarted or crashed and nobody unsealed it (Shamir seal).
An operator or automation ran `vault operator seal`.
Vault sealed itself after an unrecoverable internal error (look for the preceding ERROR line).
external_causes: Auto-unseal KMS/HSM was unreachable at startup, so the node never unsealed.
Load balancer health check is routing traffic to a sealed node.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check seal, HA and storage state of this node
Check seal type, recovery mode and unseal progress
Scroll back in the log to the first ERROR before the seal; that line is the real cause
Submit unseal key shares until the threshold is reached
For auto-unseal, verify the KMS/HSM is reachable from this host and restart Vault
Query the health endpoint on every node (200 active, 429 standby, 473 perf standby, 501 uninitialized, 503 sealed)

examples:
Error making API request.

URL: GET https://vault:8200/v1/secret/data/app
Code: 503. Errors:

* Vault is sealed

entries.title: Vault is not initialized
entries.summary: Storage contains no barrier/keyring, so Vault has never been initialized against this storage backend (or is pointed at the wrong one).
internal_causes: Brand-new cluster that has not run `vault operator init`.
Raft follower that has not joined the cluster yet.
Config `path`/`storage` stanza changed and now points at an empty location.
external_causes: Storage backend data was deleted or restored from an empty backup.
Wrong Consul/S3/DB prefix, bucket or table.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check seal, HA and storage state of this node
Review the seal / storage / listener stanzas in the server config
If this is a raft follower, join it instead of initializing
Only for a truly new cluster: initialize

examples:
Error making API request.

Code: 400. Errors:

* Vault is not initialized

entries.title: Unseal failed, invalid key
entries.summary: The combined unseal key shares did not decrypt the barrier keyring.
internal_causes: Key shares come from a different cluster or a previous `vault operator init`.
Shares from a pre-rekey set were mixed with the current ones.
Shares were mistyped or base64/hex mixed.
external_causes: Storage was restored from a backup taken after a rekey, so it expects different keys.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check seal type, recovery mode and unseal progress
Reset unseal progress and start again with shares from a single key set
Submit unseal key shares until the threshold is reached
Confirm with the key custodians which init/rekey generation the shares belong to

examples:
Error unsealing: Error making API request.

URL: PUT https://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/unseal
Code: 400. Errors:

* Unseal failed, invalid key

entries.title: Auto-unseal seal wrapper unreachable
patterns: failed to decrypt health test value
entries.summary: Vault's periodic seal health check, or startup unseal, could not complete an encrypt/decrypt round trip with the auto-unseal KMS/HSM.
internal_causes: Seal stanza has the wrong key ID, region, endpoint or mount path.
external_causes: KMS/HSM endpoint not reachable (DNS, proxy, firewall, VPC endpoint, private link).
IAM/credentials for the seal expired or were changed.
KMS key disabled, scheduled for deletion, or its key policy changed.
KMS throttling or regional outage.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check seal, HA and storage state of this node
Check the seal stanza for key id, region and endpoint
From the Vault host, confirm which IAM identity Vault is using
AWS KMS: test the key from the Vault host using Vault's credentials
Confirm network reachability to the KMS endpoint
Stream server logs at debug level without a restart

examples: 2024-05-01T10:00:00.000Z [WARN]  core: seal health check failed: error="failed to encrypt test value, seal wrapper may be unreachable: context deadline exceeded"

entries.title: AWS KMS auto-unseal error
patterns: error initializing AWS KMS wrapping client
error fetching AWS KMS wrapping key information
key id not found in env or config for aws kms wrapper
entries.summary: Vault could not use the AWS KMS key configured in `seal "awskms"`.
internal_causes: `kms_key_id`, `region` or `endpoint` is wrong in the seal stanza.
external_causes: IAM role/instance profile lacks kms:Encrypt, kms:Decrypt or kms:DescribeKey.
KMS key policy does not trust Vault's IAM principal.
Key is disabled or pending deletion (KMSInvalidStateException).
No route to KMS (missing VPC endpoint, proxy, SCP or firewall).

troubleshooting_steps.step: From the Vault host, confirm which IAM identity Vault is using
Describe the key and check KeyState is Enabled
Test encrypt with Vault's credentials
Review the key policy for Vault's role
Check CloudTrail for denied kms:Decrypt / kms:Encrypt calls from Vault's role
Check seal, HA and storage state of this node

examples: [ERROR] core: failed to unseal: error="error fetching AWS KMS wrapping key information: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/vault/i-0abc is not authorized to perform: kms:DescribeKey"

entries.title: Azure Key Vault auto-unseal error
patterns: error initializing Azure Key Vault wrapper client
error fetching Azure Key Vault wrapper key information
failed to acquire managed identity credentials
failed to get client secret credentials
entries.summary: Vault could not authenticate to, or read the key from, Azure Key Vault for auto-unseal.
internal_causes: `vault_name`, `key_name`, `tenant_id` or `environment` wrong in the seal stanza.
external_causes: Managed identity not assigned to the VM/pod, or client secret expired.
Key Vault access policy / RBAC lacks get, wrapKey and unwrapKey.
Key Vault firewall or private endpoint blocks the Vault host.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Confirm the identity can read the key
Check access policies / role assignments for wrapKey and unwrapKey
Check the Key Vault network rules
Check seal, HA and storage state of this node

examples: [ERROR] core: failed to unseal: error="error fetching Azure Key Vault wrapper key information: keyvault.BaseClient#GetKey: Failure responding to request: StatusCode=403"

entries.title: GCP Cloud KMS auto-unseal error
patterns: error initializing GCP CKMS wrapper client
'(crypto_key|key_ring|project|region)' not found for GCP CKMS wrapper configuration
entries.summary: Vault could not reach or use the Google Cloud KMS key configured in `seal "gcpckms"`.
internal_causes: `project`, `region`, `key_ring` or `crypto_key` missing or wrong in the seal stanza.
external_causes: Service account lacks roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the key.
GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS not readable by the vault user.
Key version disabled or destroyed.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Describe the crypto key and check the primary version state
Check IAM bindings on the key
Check seal, HA and storage state of this node

examples: Error parsing Seal configuration: 'crypto_key' not found for GCP CKMS wrapper configuration

entries.title: Transit auto-unseal error
patterns: after (en|de)crypt operation .*(returned from vault|returned secret from vault)
error (en|de)crypting data: Error making API request
entries.summary: Vault could not use the remote Vault Transit key that unseals this cluster.
internal_causes: `address`, `mount_path` or `key_name` wrong in the seal stanza.
external_causes: The transit cluster is sealed, down or unreachable.
The seal token expired or was revoked (it must be a periodic or long-lived token).
Token policy lacks update on transit/encrypt/<key> and transit/decrypt/<key>.
TLS CA/client cert for the transit cluster is invalid.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check the transit (unsealer) cluster health
Check the seal token TTL and policies on the transit cluster
Confirm the key exists
Check seal, HA and storage state of this node

examples:
[ERROR] core: failed to unseal: error="error decrypting data: Error making API request.

URL: PUT https://transit-vault:8200/v1/transit/decrypt/autounseal
Code: 403. Errors:

* permission denied"

entries.title: HSM (PKCS#11) seal error
entries.summary: The Enterprise PKCS#11 seal received an error from the HSM library (CKR_* return codes come from the HSM).
internal_causes: Wrong `lib`, `slot`/`token_label`, `pin`, `key_label` or mechanism in the seal stanza.
external_causes: HSM unreachable or partition offline (network HSM).
HSM client software version mismatch or session limit reached.
PIN locked/expired (CKR_PIN_INCORRECT, CKR_PIN_LOCKED).
Key not found in the partition (CKR_KEY_HANDLE_INVALID / CKR_OBJECT_HANDLE_INVALID).

troubleshooting_steps.step: List slots/tokens visible to the Vault host
Log in and list objects with the configured PIN
Check the HSM vendor client logs and connectivity
Check seal, HA and storage state of this node

examples: [ERROR] core: failed to unseal: error="error decrypting data: pkcs11: 0x30: CKR_DEVICE_ERROR"

source.note: HSM PKCS#11 return codes (Vault Enterprise HSM seal)

entries.title: Seal migration required / pending
patterns: migrate option not provided and seal migration is pending
cannot run in recovery mode when a seal migration is needed
entries.summary: The seal in the config differs from the seal that protects the data in storage, and Vault will not switch until a seal migration is run.
internal_causes: Seal stanza changed (Shamir to auto-unseal, auto-unseal to Shamir, or KMS to KMS) without `disabled = "true"` on the old seal.
Not every node got the same config change.
Migration started but was not finished on all nodes.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Review the seal / storage / listener stanzas in the server config
Check seal type, recovery mode and unseal progress
Keep the old seal in the config with disabled = "true" next to the new seal, then restart Vault
Unseal with -migrate on each node (standbys first, then the active node)
Check seal, HA and storage state of this node

examples: [WARN]  core: migrate option not provided and seal migration is pending

entries.title: Neither old nor new seal can read stored keys
patterns: neither the old nor new seal can read stored keys
decrypt error, neither the old nor new seal
entries.summary: During seal migration Vault tried both seals and neither could decrypt the stored keys.
internal_causes: Both seal stanzas point at the wrong keys.
Storage was restored from a different cluster.
external_causes: The old KMS key was deleted or disabled before migration finished.
Credentials for either KMS are invalid.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Review the seal / storage / listener stanzas in the server config
Verify both KMS keys are enabled and accessible with Vault's credentials
Check seal type, recovery mode and unseal progress
Stream server logs at debug level without a restart

examples: Error unsealing: neither the old nor new seal can read stored keys: old seal err=AccessDeniedException, new seal err=<nil>

entries.title: Newer seal generation found in storage
patterns: seal configuration in this node should be updated to match
entries.summary: Another node changed the seal configuration (multi-seal / seal HA) and this node's config is out of date.
internal_causes: Seal stanzas differ between nodes after a seal config change.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Diff the seal stanzas across all nodes
Copy the config from the previous active node, then restart this node
Check seal, HA and storage state of this node

examples: [ERROR] core: A newer seal generation was found in storage. The seal configuration in this node should be updated to match that of the previous active node, and this node should be restarted.

entries.title: Seal decrypt failed
patterns: value has no key-id in common with currently healthy seals
entries.summary: A seal-wrapped value could not be decrypted with the configured seal key(s).
internal_causes: Seal config points to a different key than the one that wrapped the data.
external_causes: KMS key was rotated with old versions disabled, or the key was replaced.
KMS denied decrypt (IAM/key policy) or the KMS is unreachable.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Review the seal / storage / listener stanzas in the server config
Check KMS audit logs (CloudTrail / Azure Monitor / Cloud Audit Logs) for failed Decrypt calls
Check seal, HA and storage state of this node
Stream server logs at debug level without a restart

examples: [ERROR] core: error decrypting using seal awskms: failed to decrypt envelope: cipher: message authentication failed

entries.title: Barrier initialized but seal configuration missing
patterns: barrier reports initialized but no seal configuration found
Recovery seal configuration not found for existing seal
entries.summary: Storage has a keyring but the seal/recovery configuration entries are missing or unreadable.
internal_causes: Partial restore or manual edits of core/ storage paths.
external_causes: Storage backend returned partial data (eventual consistency, wrong prefix).
Backup restore missing core/seal-config or core/recovery-config.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Run offline checks of config, listener TLS, storage and seal
Review the seal / storage / listener stanzas in the server config
Contact HashiCorp support before changing storage; collect a storage listing of core/

examples: [ERROR] core: barrier reports initialized but no seal configuration found

entries.title: Cannot seal a standby node
patterns: vault cannot seal when in standby mode
entries.summary: `vault operator seal` was sent to a standby. Only the active node can be sealed through the API.
internal_causes: Request reached a standby node directly or through a load balancer.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check seal, HA and storage state of this node
Send the seal request to the active node, or restart/stop the standby instead

examples:
Error sealing: Error making API request.

Code: 500. Errors:

* vault cannot seal when in standby mode; please restart instead

entries.title: Failed to lock memory (mlock)
entries.summary: Vault could not mlock its memory at startup, so it refuses to start rather than risk swapping secrets to disk.
internal_causes: `disable_mlock` not set where mlock is unsupported.
external_causes: Missing IPC_LOCK capability (containers) or CAP_IPC_LOCK on the binary.
LimitMEMLOCK too low in the systemd unit.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Grant the capability to the binary
Check the systemd unit for LimitMEMLOCK=infinity and AmbientCapabilities=CAP_IPC_LOCK
With integrated storage, HashiCorp recommends disable_mlock = true

examples:
Error initializing core: Failed to lock memory: cannot allocate memory

This usually means that the mlock syscall is not available.

entries.title: Raft heartbeat timeout and election
entries.summary: A follower stopped hearing from the leader and started an election. Occasional elections are normal; repeated ones mean the cluster is unstable.
internal_causes: Leader overloaded (large snapshots, heavy write load, GC pauses).
Mismatched `performance_multiplier` across nodes.
external_causes: Network latency, packet loss or partition on port 8201.
Slow disk (fsync latency) on the leader or follower.
VM CPU steal or noisy neighbors.

troubleshooting_steps.step: List raft peers; confirm one leader and that all voters are present
Check autopilot health, last contact and log index of each server
Verify API (8200) and cluster (8201) ports are reachable between every pair of nodes
Check disk latency on the raft data volume
Check vault.raft metrics (commitTime, leader.lastContact)
Stream server logs at debug level without a restart

examples: 2024-05-01T10:00:00.000Z [WARN]  storage.raft: heartbeat timeout reached, starting election: last-leader-addr=10.0.0.11:8201 last-leader-id=vault-1

entries.title: Raft lost quorum
patterns: failed to contact quorum of nodes
not part of (a )?stable configuration, aborting election
entries.summary: The leader could not reach a majority of voters and stepped down, or no node can win an election. Writes stop until quorum returns.
internal_causes: Too many voters removed or failed (for example 2 of 3).
Nodes removed from the configuration but still running.
external_causes: Network partition between availability zones or a firewall change on port 8201.
Hosts down, disks full, or pods rescheduled with lost volumes.

troubleshooting_steps.step: List raft peers; confirm one leader and that all voters are present
Query the health endpoint on every node (200 active, 429 standby, 473 perf standby, 501 uninitialized, 503 sealed)
Verify API (8200) and cluster (8201) ports are reachable between every pair of nodes
Check disk space on the raft data directory
If quorum cannot come back, follow the lost-quorum procedure with peers.json

examples: [WARN]  storage.raft: failed to contact quorum of nodes, stepping down

entries.title: Raft replication/heartbeat RPC failures
entries.summary: The raft leader cannot send log entries or heartbeats to a peer over the cluster port.
internal_causes: `cluster_addr` advertises an address other nodes cannot reach (NAT, 0.0.0.0, container IP).
external_causes: Firewall or security group blocking 8201.
Peer down or restarting.
TLS interception or a proxy on the cluster port (raft uses mTLS that Vault manages).

troubleshooting_steps.step: List raft peers; confirm one leader and that all voters are present
Verify API (8200) and cluster (8201) ports are reachable between every pair of nodes
Check cluster_addr / api_addr in the config of the failing peer
Check autopilot health, last contact and log index of each server

examples: [ERROR] storage.raft: failed to appendEntries to: peer="{Voter vault-2 10.0.0.12:8201}" error="dial tcp 10.0.0.12:8201: connect: connection refused"

entries.title: Raft rejecting vote requests
patterns: rejecting (pre-)?vote request since (we have a leader|node is not in configuration|node is not a voter|our last (index|term) is greater)
entries.summary: A node that is not part of the current configuration, or is behind, keeps asking for votes. Usually a removed or rejoined node that still has old raft data.
internal_causes: Node removed with `remove-peer` but still running with old data.
Node restored from an old disk/snapshot, so its term/index is behind.
Duplicate node_id across nodes.

troubleshooting_steps.step: List raft peers; confirm one leader and that all voters are present
Check node_id in each node's raft stanza is unique
A single 'since we have a leader' message during an election is normal; act only if it repeats
If the node is not in the configuration and should be, rejoin it
Only for a node that was removed with remove-peer or restored from an old disk: stop it, move its raft data dir aside, then rejoin

examples: [WARN]  storage.raft: rejecting vote request since node is not in configuration: from=10.0.0.14:8201

entries.title: Raft join failed
patterns: must provide leader address or auto-join metadata
failed to create tls config to communicate with leader node
too many concurrent raft retry joins
entries.summary: A node could not join the raft cluster through `retry_join` or `vault operator raft join`.
internal_causes: `leader_api_addr` wrong or uses http where the leader serves https.
`leader_ca_cert_file` / `leader_tls_servername` do not match the leader's API certificate.
Node already has raft data from another cluster.
external_causes: Leader API port 8200 not reachable from the joining node.
DNS for the leader address does not resolve.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Test the leader API from the joining node
Review the retry_join stanza
List raft peers; confirm one leader and that all voters are present
Stream server logs at debug level without a restart

examples: [ERROR] core: failed to retry join raft cluster: retry=2s err="failed to create tls config to communicate with leader node \"https://vault-0.vault-internal:8200\": open /vault/tls/ca.crt: no such file or directory"

Error joining the node to the Raft cluster: Error making API request.

Code: 500. Errors:

* failed to join raft cluster: context deadline exceeded

entries.title: Raft bootstrap challenge failed
patterns: too many raft challenges in flight
failed to send answer to raft leader node
could not retrieve raft bootstrap package
entries.summary: During join the follower must decrypt a challenge from the leader using the shared seal. That exchange failed.
internal_causes: Follower is configured with a different seal or KMS key than the leader.
Shamir follower was not unsealed with the cluster's unseal keys after join.
external_causes: Follower cannot reach the leader's API address (load balancer, TLS SNI, firewall).
Follower cannot reach the KMS to decrypt the challenge.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Compare the seal stanza on leader and follower
Test the leader API from the follower
For Shamir seals, unseal the follower after it joins
Check seal, HA and storage state of this node

examples:
[ERROR] core: failed to retry join raft cluster: err="failed to get raft challenge: Error making API request.

URL: POST https://vault-0:8200/v1/sys/storage/raft/bootstrap/challenge
Code: 503"

entries.title: Node seal state wrong for raft join
patterns: node must be unsealed to bootstrap
can't perform a seal migration while joining a raft cluster
incompatible seal types between raft leader
entries.summary: Raft join requires a specific seal state, or the follower's seal type differs from the leader's.
internal_causes: Joining a node that is already unsealed against other storage.
Follower uses Shamir while the leader uses auto-unseal (or the reverse).

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check seal, HA and storage state of this node
Review the seal / storage / listener stanzas in the server config
'must be unsealed': unseal the node, then retry the join
'must be sealed before joining': the node already unsealed against other storage; restart it with the raft storage stanza, then join
'incompatible seal types': align the seal stanza with the leader, then restart and rejoin

examples:
Error joining the node to the Raft cluster: Code: 500. Errors:

* node must be sealed before joining

entries.title: Raft node removed / stale data
patterns: raft data for this node must be cleaned up before it can be added back
node has been removed from the HA cluster
entries.summary: The node's raft directory belongs to an old membership (it was removed), or the node was already initialized.
internal_causes: `vault operator raft remove-peer` was run, then the node was restarted with its old data.
Re-using a volume from another cluster.

troubleshooting_steps.step: List raft peers; confirm one leader and that all voters are present
Stop Vault, move the raft data directory away, then start and rejoin
troubleshooting_steps.command: sudo systemctl stop vault && sudo mv /opt/vault/data /opt/vault/data.bak && sudo systemctl start vault

troubleshooting_steps.step: Rejoin the node

examples: [ERROR] core: node has been removed from the HA cluster. Raft data for this node must be cleaned up before it can be added back

entries.title: Raft snapshot from a different seal
patterns: could not verify hash file, possibly the snapshot is using a different (autoseal key|set of unseal keys)
entries.summary: The snapshot was taken on a cluster with a different seal/unseal keys, so its integrity hash cannot be checked.
internal_causes: Restoring a snapshot from another cluster (DR test, migration) or from before a rekey.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Confirm where the snapshot came from and which seal it was taken with
If you intend to restore it, use force; the target then needs the source cluster's unseal/recovery keys
troubleshooting_steps.command: vault operator raft snapshot restore -force backup.snap

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check seal, HA and storage state of this node

examples:
Error installing the snapshot: Code: 400. Errors:

* could not verify hash file, possibly the snapshot is using a different set of unseal keys; use the snapshot-force API to bypass this check

entries.title: Raft snapshot install / write failure
patterns: failed to move snapshot into place
entries.summary: Raft could not create, move or install a snapshot on local disk.
internal_causes: Corrupt or truncated snapshot file supplied to restore.
external_causes: Disk full or slow on the raft data volume.
Wrong ownership/permissions on the snapshots directory.
Read-only filesystem or SELinux/AppArmor denial.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check free space and inodes
Check ownership of the raft directory
Look for kernel or filesystem errors
List raft peers; confirm one leader and that all voters are present

examples: [ERROR] storage.raft: failed to install snapshot: error="failed to move snapshot into place: rename: no space left on device"

entries.title: Raft peers.json recovery failed
patterns: raft recovery failed to parse peers\.json
entries.summary: Vault found a `raft/peers.json` file at startup but could not use it for manual recovery.
internal_causes: Malformed JSON, wrong node IDs or addresses in peers.json.
peers.json copied to only some nodes.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Validate the file
Confirm each id matches the node_id and each address is the cluster address (host:8201)
Place an identical peers.json on every surviving node, then restart them

examples: [ERROR] core: raft recovery failed to parse peers.json: invalid character '}' looking for beginning of object key string

entries.title: Raft entry too large
patterns: retrieved entry value is too large
put failed due to value being too large
entries.summary: A storage entry exceeds raft `max_entry_size` (default 1 MiB), often the mount table or a large KV secret.
internal_causes: Very many mounts/namespaces make the mount table too large.
Clients write very large KV values.
max_entry_size was lowered after data was written.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check the configured limits in the raft stanza
Find the large writes in the audit log
Raise max_entry_size on all nodes consistently, or reduce payload size

examples: [ERROR] core: retrieved entry value is too large, has raft's max_entry_size or max_mount_and_namespace_table_entry_size been reduced?

entries.title: Raft FSM / data file problems
patterns: raft FSM db file has wider permissions than needed
error checking raft FSM db file
failed to check if raft\.db already exists
MAP_POPULATE mmap flag has not been set
entries.summary: Vault found unexpected permissions, size or access problems on the raft vault.db / raft.db files.
external_causes: Data files owned by root or world-readable after manual copy/restore.
Database larger than available memory (slow startup).

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check file modes and owner
Fix ownership and modes
Check memory against database size

examples: [WARN]  storage.raft.fsm: raft FSM db file has wider permissions than needed: needed=-rw------- existing=-rw-r--r--

entries.title: Raft storage not initialized / shut down
patterns: raft storage is not in use
raft storage autopilot is not initialized
entries.summary: A raft operation was called while raft is not running on this node, or the cluster uses a different storage backend.
internal_causes: Running `vault operator raft` commands against a Consul-backed cluster.
Node is still starting, sealed or not yet joined.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check seal, HA and storage state of this node
Confirm storage type (Storage Type line)
List raft peers; confirm one leader and that all voters are present

examples:
Error reading the raft cluster configuration: Code: 500. Errors:

* raft storage is not initialized

entries.title: Raft cluster_addr is unspecified
patterns: cannot use unspecified IP with raft storage
entries.summary: `cluster_addr` resolves to 0.0.0.0 or `::`, which peers cannot dial.
internal_causes: cluster_addr set to 0.0.0.0, or derived from a listener bound to all interfaces.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Set cluster_addr to a routable address on every node
Restart and verify

examples: Error initializing storage of type raft: cannot use unspecified IP with raft storage: 0.0.0.0:8201

entries.title: Raft TLS keyring problems
patterns: could not find raft TLS configuration
could not decode raft TLS configuration
failed to read raft TLS keyring
no active raft TLS key found
got raft connection but no local cert
raft tls periodic upgrade check failed
entries.summary: Vault manages its own mTLS keyring for raft cluster traffic, and it could not load or rotate it.
internal_causes: Node not fully unsealed when raft traffic arrived.
Keyring storage entry damaged after partial restore.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check seal, HA and storage state of this node
List raft peers; confirm one leader and that all voters are present
Stream server logs at debug level without a restart

examples: [ERROR] storage.raft: no active raft TLS key found

entries.title: Raft cloud auto-join discovery failed
patterns: failed to parse addresses from auto-join metadata
entries.summary: `retry_join { auto_join = "provider=..." }` could not list peers through the cloud provider API.
internal_causes: Malformed auto_join string (provider, tag_key, tag_value, region).
external_causes: IAM role lacks ec2:DescribeInstances (AWS) or the equivalent on Azure/GCP.
Instances do not carry the expected tags.
No route to the cloud metadata or API endpoint.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Review the auto_join string
From the Vault host, confirm which IAM identity Vault is using
Confirm instances are discoverable by tag

examples: [ERROR] core: failed to retry join raft cluster: error="failed to parse addresses from auto-join metadata: discover-aws: DescribeInstances failed: UnauthorizedOperation"

entries.title: Consul session / HA lock lost
patterns: failed to renew consul session for more than the TTL, lock lost
session check failed on write, we lost active node lock
entries.summary: The active node lost its Consul lock, stepped down, and a standby took over (leadership flapping if repeated).
internal_causes: `session_ttl` / `lock_wait_time` too aggressive for the environment.
external_causes: Consul agent on the Vault host unhealthy or restarting.
Consul servers lost leader or are overloaded.
Network latency between Vault, the agent and the Consul servers.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check the local Consul agent and cluster members
Check Consul raft health
Look for session invalidations in the Consul agent logs
Check seal, HA and storage state of this node

examples: [WARN]  storage.consul: session check failed on write, we lost active node lock, stepping down

entries.title: Consul storage access/ACL error
patterns: rpc error making call: Permission denied
key or cert path: .* cannot be loaded from consul config file
entries.summary: Vault could not read or write its Consul KV prefix.
internal_causes: Wrong `address`, `scheme`, `path` or TLS files in the consul storage stanza.
external_causes: Consul ACL token missing, expired or lacking key_prefix/session write.
Consul agent not listening on the configured address.
Consul TLS/mTLS required but not configured.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Test the token against Consul directly
troubleshooting_steps.command: CONSUL_HTTP_TOKEN=<token> consul kv get -recurse vault/ | head

troubleshooting_steps.step: Inspect the ACL token's policies
Confirm agent reachability

examples: [ERROR] core: failed to check for initialization: error="Unexpected response code: 403 (ACL not found)"

entries.title: etcd storage error
patterns: failed to discover etcd endpoints through SRV discovery
etcdserver: (request timed out|mvcc: database space exceeded|leader changed|no leader)
entries.summary: Vault's etcd backend could not reach etcd, or etcd rejected the request.
internal_causes: Wrong `address` / `etcd_api` / TLS settings in the storage stanza.
external_causes: etcd quota exceeded (needs compaction and defrag).
etcd cluster lost leader or is slow (disk fsync).
Network or TLS problems to the etcd endpoints.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check etcd endpoint health
Check status, DB size and alarms
troubleshooting_steps.command: etcdctl --endpoints=<endpoints> endpoint status -w table && etcdctl alarm list

examples: [ERROR] core: error="etcdserver: mvcc: database space exceeded"

entries.title: DynamoDB storage error
entries.summary: Vault's DynamoDB backend was throttled, denied, or could not find its table.
internal_causes: Wrong `table`, `region` or `endpoint`; ha_enabled without suitable settings.
external_causes: Table capacity too low (provisioned mode) causing throttling.
IAM policy missing dynamodb:GetItem/PutItem/DeleteItem/Query/DescribeTable on the table.
Credentials not available (no instance profile / env).

troubleshooting_steps.step: From the Vault host, confirm which IAM identity Vault is using
Describe the table and capacity
Check ThrottledRequests and ConsumedWriteCapacity metrics in CloudWatch for the table

examples: [ERROR] core: error="ProvisionedThroughputExceededException: The level of configured provisioned throughput for the table was exceeded"

entries.title: S3 storage error
patterns: unable to access bucket .* in region
entries.summary: Vault could not access the configured S3 bucket.
internal_causes: Wrong `bucket`, `region` or `endpoint` (S3-compatible stores).
`s3_force_path_style` needed for MinIO-type endpoints.
external_causes: IAM/bucket policy lacks s3:ListBucket, s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject, s3:DeleteObject.
Bucket in another region, or blocked by VPC endpoint policy or SCP.

troubleshooting_steps.step: From the Vault host, confirm which IAM identity Vault is using
List the bucket with Vault's credentials
Review the bucket policy

examples: Error initializing storage of type s3: unable to access bucket "vault-data" in region "us-east-1": AccessDenied: Access Denied

entries.title: PostgreSQL storage error
entries.summary: Vault's PostgreSQL backend could not connect, authenticate, or find its tables.
internal_causes: `connection_url`, `table` or `ha_table` wrong in the storage stanza.
external_causes: DB credentials rotated or wrong.
Tables vault_kv_store / vault_ha_locks not created (Vault does not create them).
pg_hba.conf, network or TLS (sslmode) blocking the connection.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Connect with the same URL from the Vault host
Create the required tables if missing (see the PostgreSQL storage docs)

examples: Error initializing storage of type postgresql: failed to connect to postgres: pq: password authentication failed for user "vault"

entries.title: MySQL storage error
patterns: mysql: (unable to update DB with new leader information|getting global lock id failed|lock already held)
entries.summary: Vault's MySQL backend could not connect, create its schema, or take the HA lock.
internal_causes: Wrong `address`, `database`, `table` or TLS (`tls_ca_file`) settings.
external_causes: Invalid credentials or missing grants (CREATE, SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE).
Network or TLS problem to the MySQL server.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Connect from the Vault host
Review the seal / storage / listener stanzas in the server config

examples: Error initializing storage of type mysql: failed to connect to mysql: Error 1045: Access denied for user 'vault'@'10.0.0.5'

entries.title: Google Cloud Storage backend error
entries.summary: Vault's GCS backend could not create a client or access the bucket.
internal_causes: Wrong bucket name or missing HA settings.
external_causes: Service account lacks storage.objects.* on the bucket.
Credentials file not readable by the vault user.

troubleshooting_steps.step: List the bucket with Vault's identity
Check bucket IAM

examples: Error initializing storage of type gcs: failed to create storage client: dialing: google: could not find default credentials

entries.title: Azure storage backend error
patterns: failed to obtain auth token from IMDS
entries.summary: Vault's Azure Blob storage backend could not authenticate or access the container.
internal_causes: Wrong accountName/container/environment in the storage stanza.
external_causes: Managed identity not assigned or lacks Storage Blob Data Contributor.
Storage account firewall blocks the Vault host.
IMDS unreachable from the container.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check access with Vault's identity
Check IMDS from the host

examples: Error initializing storage of type azure: failed to get properties for container "vault": StatusCode=403

entries.title: Cannot write to read-only storage
entries.summary: A write reached a read-only storage view, for example on a performance secondary, a DR secondary or during recovery mode.
internal_causes: Writing to a replicated mount on a performance secondary that is not forwarded.
Node in recovery mode.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check seal, HA and storage state of this node
Check replication mode of this cluster
Send the write to the primary, or mark the mount local if intended

examples:
Error writing data to secret/foo: Code: 500. Errors:

* cannot write to readonly storage

entries.title: HA lock acquisition failure
entries.summary: The node could not acquire or keep the HA lock in the storage/HA backend, so it stays standby or steps down.
internal_causes: Two clusters pointed at the same storage path.
Clock skew affecting lock TTLs.
external_causes: Storage/HA backend slow or unavailable (Consul, etcd, DynamoDB, ZooKeeper, DB).
Network latency to the HA backend.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check seal, HA and storage state of this node
Query the health endpoint on every node (200 active, 429 standby, 473 perf standby, 501 uninitialized, 503 sealed)
Check the HA backend health with its own tooling (consul members, etcdctl endpoint health, ...)
Stream server logs at debug level without a restart

examples: [ERROR] core: failed to acquire lock: error="context deadline exceeded"

entries.title: Storage request timed out
patterns: failed to persist keyring: context deadline exceeded
entries.summary: A storage operation did not finish before its context deadline. Vault is waiting on the storage layer.
internal_causes: Very large lease counts or mount tables slow down startup/unseal.
Raft leader overloaded.
external_causes: Storage backend latency (disk fsync, network, throttling).
Network partition to the backend.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check seal, HA and storage state of this node
Check storage latency metrics (vault.<backend>.get/put)
Check disk latency on raft nodes
Stream server logs at debug level without a restart

examples: [ERROR] core: failed to persist keyring: context deadline exceeded

source.note: Go context deadline surfaced by the storage backend client

entries.title: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
patterns: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
entries.summary: The client (CLI, agent, app, peer node or plugin) does not trust the CA that signed Vault's (or the remote service's) certificate.
internal_causes: `VAULT_CACERT` / `ca_cert` / `leader_ca_cert_file` not set.
external_causes: Private CA not in the system trust store.
TLS-intercepting proxy or load balancer presents its own certificate.
Intermediate certificate missing from the server chain.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Inspect the chain the server actually presents
Point the client at the CA bundle
Verify the server cert against the CA

examples: Error checking seal status: Get "https://vault.example.com:8200/v1/sys/seal-status": tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority

entries.title: x509: certificate name mismatch
patterns: x509: certificate is valid for .*, not
x509: certificate is not valid for any names
entries.summary: The certificate's SANs do not include the hostname or IP the client used.
internal_causes: `api_addr` / `leader_api_addr` / `leader_tls_servername` use a name not in the cert.
external_causes: Certificate issued without the load balancer DNS name or node IPs.
Client connects by IP while the cert has only DNS SANs.

troubleshooting_steps.step: List SANs on the served certificate
Use a matching hostname, set VAULT_TLS_SERVER_NAME, or reissue the cert with the right SANs

examples: Error making API request: Get "https://10.0.0.11:8200/v1/sys/health": x509: cannot validate certificate for 10.0.0.11 because it doesn't contain any IP SANs

entries.title: x509: certificate expired
patterns: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid
entries.summary: A certificate in the chain is expired or not yet valid. Check the system clock too.
external_causes: Listener cert or intermediate expired.
System clock skew on client or server (NTP).
Upstream service (KMS proxy, LDAP, DB) cert expired.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check validity dates
Check clock sync
Replace the cert and reload the listener without restart

examples: [ERROR] core: error="x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid: current time 2024-05-01T10:00:00Z is after 2024-04-30T00:00:00Z"

entries.title: HTTP/HTTPS scheme mismatch
patterns: server gave HTTP response to HTTPS client
client sent an HTTP request to an HTTPS server
entries.summary: Client and server disagree on TLS: one side uses http:// and the other https://.
internal_causes: Listener has `tls_disable = true` while VAULT_ADDR uses https (or the reverse).
`api_addr` / `leader_api_addr` uses the wrong scheme.
external_causes: Load balancer terminates TLS and forwards plain HTTP (or the reverse).

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check VAULT_ADDR scheme
Check the listener's tls_disable
Test both schemes

examples: Error checking seal status: Get "https://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/seal-status": http: server gave HTTP response to HTTPS client

entries.title: TLS handshake failure
patterns: remote error: tls: (bad certificate|unknown certificate authority|handshake failure|protocol version)
entries.summary: A TLS handshake to the listener failed: client cert required, version/cipher mismatch, or an untrusted client.
internal_causes: `tls_require_and_verify_client_cert` enabled but clients send no cert.
`tls_min_version` / `tls_cipher_suites` too strict for the clients.
external_causes: Load balancer health checks over plain TCP/HTTP (noisy but harmless).
Old client TLS stack.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Identify the source IPs in the log lines (LB health checks are common)
Test the handshake and negotiated protocol
Review listener TLS options

examples: 2024-05-01T10:00:00.000Z [INFO]  http: TLS handshake error from 10.0.1.5:51544: remote error: tls: bad certificate

entries.title: Listener TLS configuration error
patterns: 'tls_max_version' must be greater than or equal to 'tls_min_version'
failed to (read|parse CA certificate in) tls_client_ca_file
tls: private key does not match public key
entries.summary: Vault could not build the listener TLS config from the files and options in the listener stanza.
internal_causes: Wrong tls_cert_file / tls_key_file paths, key/cert mismatch, or PEM order (leaf first, then intermediates).
Invalid or conflicting tls_* options.
external_causes: Files not readable by the vault user (permissions, SELinux).

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check that key and cert match
troubleshooting_steps.command: c=$(openssl x509 -noout -pubkey -in vault.crt) && k=$(openssl pkey -pubout -in vault.key) && [ "$c" = "$k" ] && echo match || echo MISMATCH-or-unreadable

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check file permissions for the vault user
Run offline checks of config, listener TLS, storage and seal

examples: Error initializing listener of type tcp: error loading TLS cert: open /etc/vault.d/tls/vault.crt: permission denied

entries.title: Active node not found
patterns: local node not active but active cluster node not found
Vault is not configured for highly-available mode
entries.summary: A standby received a request but does not know which node is active, so it cannot forward.
internal_causes: Election in progress or leadership flapping.
`api_addr` / `cluster_addr` advertise unreachable addresses.
external_causes: HA/storage backend unhealthy, so no node holds the lock.
Cluster port 8201 blocked between nodes.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check seal, HA and storage state of this node
Query the health endpoint on every node (200 active, 429 standby, 473 perf standby, 501 uninitialized, 503 sealed)
List raft peers; confirm one leader and that all voters are present
Verify API (8200) and cluster (8201) ports are reachable between every pair of nodes
Check which node holds leadership

examples:
Error making API request.

Code: 500. Errors:

* local node not active but active cluster node not found

entries.title: Standby request forwarding failed
patterns: cannot forward request; no connection or address not known
err setting up forwarding rpc client
error parsing cluster address attempting to refresh forwarding connection
entries.summary: A standby could not forward a client request to the active node over the cluster port (gRPC on 8201).
internal_causes: `cluster_addr` of the active node is unreachable from standbys.
external_causes: Firewall/security group blocks 8201.
Load balancer or proxy in front of 8201 (it must be direct TCP).
Active node changed and connections are being re-established.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check seal, HA and storage state of this node
Check leader and its cluster address
Verify API (8200) and cluster (8201) ports are reachable between every pair of nodes
Stream server logs at debug level without a restart

examples: [ERROR] core: forward request error: error="error during forwarding RPC request"

entries.title: Please forward to the active node
patterns: please forward to the active node
entries.summary: A performance standby got a write it cannot handle locally. Vault normally forwards this; if a client sees it, forwarding is broken or bypassed.
internal_causes: Client talks to a perf standby with forwarding disabled.
Plugin returns the error directly.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check seal, HA and storage state of this node
Send writes to the active node through the load balancer (use sys/health?perfstandbyok for read-only pools)
Stream server logs at debug level without a restart

examples:
Code: 500. Errors:

* please forward to the active node

entries.title: Leadership lost / stepping down
patterns: audit device configuration failed, skipping HA lock acquisition
entries.summary: The active node lost leadership and stepped down, or a node cannot become active.
internal_causes: Post-unseal setup failed (for example an audit device could not start), so Vault will not take the lock.
Manual step-down.
external_causes: Storage/HA backend lost the lock or quorum.
Audit sink (file/socket/syslog) not available.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check seal, HA and storage state of this node
List raft peers; confirm one leader and that all voters are present
Check the log lines right before the step-down for the real error
If an audit device failed, check its file path/socket

examples: [WARN]  core: leadership lost, stopping active operation

entries.title: Cluster listener / cluster TLS error
patterns: clustering not disabled but no addresses to listen on
failed to get tls configuration when starting cluster listener
entries.summary: Vault could not start the cluster (8201) listener or load its internal cluster certificate.
internal_causes: `cluster_addr` missing or not matching a listener address.
Node not unsealed yet, so cluster certificates are not loaded.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Review the seal / storage / listener stanzas in the server config
Check seal, HA and storage state of this node
Confirm something listens on the cluster port

examples: [ERROR] core: clustering not disabled but no addresses to listen on

entries.title: X-Forwarded-For rejected
patterns: client address not authorized for x-forwarded-for
missing x-forwarded-for header and configured to reject
entries.summary: The listener's X-Forwarded-For settings rejected the request from the load balancer.
internal_causes: `x_forwarded_for_authorized_addrs` missing the LB's subnet.
`x_forwarded_for_reject_not_present` set while some paths bypass the LB.
external_causes: Load balancer not adding the header, or adding multiple hops.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Review x_forwarded_for_* settings on the listener
Confirm LB source IPs and header behaviour

examples:
Code: 403. Errors:

* client address not authorized for x-forwarded-for and configured to reject connection

entries.title: Connection refused / timeout reaching Vault
patterns: dial tcp: lookup .*: no such host
entries.summary: The client could not open a TCP connection. Vault is down, listening elsewhere, or the network path is blocked.
internal_causes: VAULT_ADDR points at the wrong host/port.
Listener bound to 127.0.0.1 only.
external_causes: Vault process not running or crash-looping.
Firewall, security group or Kubernetes Service/NetworkPolicy blocking the port.
DNS failure.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check VAULT_ADDR
Check the process and listening sockets on the server
Test the path from the client
Collect the full server log around the event

examples: Error checking seal status: Get "https://vault:8200/v1/sys/seal-status": dial tcp 10.0.0.11:8200: connect: connection refused

entries.title: Too many open files
entries.summary: Vault hit the file descriptor limit, so it cannot accept connections or open storage files.
internal_causes: Client connection leak (no keep-alive reuse) or very many leases/plugins.
external_causes: LimitNOFILE too low in the systemd unit / container.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check limits and current usage
troubleshooting_steps.command: cat /proc/$(pidof vault)/limits | grep 'open files'; ls /proc/$(pidof vault)/fd | wc -l

troubleshooting_steps.step: Raise LimitNOFILE (e.g. 65536) in the unit and restart

examples: [ERROR] http: Accept error: accept tcp [::]:8200: accept4: too many open files; retrying in 1s

entries.title: Plugin process failed to start
patterns: plugin exited before we could connect
entries.summary: An external plugin binary failed to start or speak the plugin protocol.
internal_causes: Plugin registered with the wrong SHA256 or not registered after upgrade.
`plugin_directory` wrong.
external_causes: Binary built for another OS/arch, missing libraries (e.g. Oracle Instant Client), or noexec mount.
mlock or memory limits killing the plugin.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check the registration
Recompute the checksum and compare
Run the binary by hand as the vault user to see linker errors

examples:
[ERROR] secrets.database.database_1234: error creating database object: error="Unrecognized remote plugin message: 

This usually means that the plugin is either invalid or simply
needs to be recompiled to support the latest protocol."

entries.title: Listener cannot bind its address
patterns: listen tcp .*: bind: (permission denied|address already in use|cannot assign requested address)
Error initializing listener of type tcp: listen tcp
entries.summary: Vault could not open its API or cluster listener socket. This is an OS-level problem with the address or port, not a Vault token or policy problem.
internal_causes: Two listener stanzas (or api/cluster addresses) use the same port.
Listener address is an IP that does not exist on this host.
external_causes: Another process (or an old Vault) already holds the port.
Port below 1024 without CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE for the vault user.
SELinux/AppArmor denies the bind.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Find what already holds the port
Check the listener address and cluster_address in the config
For ports below 1024, add the bind capability while keeping cap_ipc_lock (setcap replaces the whole set; check getcap first)
troubleshooting_steps.command: getcap $(readlink -f $(which vault)); sudo setcap cap_ipc_lock,cap_net_bind_service=+ep $(readlink -f $(which vault))

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check SELinux denials
troubleshooting_steps.command: sudo ausearch -m avc -ts recent | grep vault

examples: Error initializing listener of type tcp: listen tcp 0.0.0.0:443: bind: permission denied
Error initializing listener of type tcp: listen tcp 0.0.0.0:8200: bind: address already in use

source.note: Go net listener bind error surfaced by Vault at startup

entries.title: Permission denied
entries.summary: The token's ACL policies do not allow the operation on that path, or the token is invalid/expired (Vault returns 403 in both cases).
internal_causes: Policy lacks the capability (read/create/update/list/sudo) on the exact path (KV v2 needs data/ and metadata/).
Token expired, revoked, or used in the wrong namespace.
Sentinel/EGP or control group denial (Enterprise).
external_causes: Client sends the wrong token (stale VAULT_TOKEN, agent cache).
Auth method backend changed group/role mapping.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Inspect the token: policies, TTL, entity, namespace
Check the token's capabilities on the exact path
Read the attached policies
Find the failing request in the audit log
troubleshooting_steps.command: jq -c 'select(.error != null) | {time, type, path: .request.path, error}' /var/log/vault/audit.log | tail -20

troubleshooting_steps.step: Confirm namespace

examples:
Error reading secret/data/app: Error making API request.

URL: GET https://vault:8200/v1/secret/data/app
Code: 403. Errors:

* permission denied

entries.title: Invalid / malformed token
entries.summary: The client sent a token that is malformed or unknown.
internal_causes: Token truncated, wrong prefix (hvs./hvb./s.), or from another cluster.
Batch token used on a cluster other than where it was created (without replication).
external_causes: Proxy or app config mangling the X-Vault-Token header.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Inspect the token: policies, TTL, entity, namespace
Log in again to get a fresh token
Find the failing request in the audit log
troubleshooting_steps.command: jq -c 'select(.error != null) | {time, type, path: .request.path, error}' /var/log/vault/audit.log | tail -20

examples:
Code: 403. Errors:

* bad token

entries.title: Lease not found / expired
patterns: cannot renew lease, no valid associated token
entries.summary: The lease ID is unknown or already expired/revoked, so it cannot be renewed or revoked.
internal_causes: App renewing after max_ttl.
Parent token revoked, which revoked child leases.
Lease from another cluster/namespace.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Look up the lease
Check the mount's default/max TTL
Inspect the token: policies, TTL, entity, namespace

examples:
Error renewing lease: Code: 400. Errors:

* lease not found

entries.title: Batch token limitations
patterns: batch tokens cannot (be renewed|be revoked|create more tokens|be root tokens)
cannot register a lease for a batch token
'token_type' cannot be 'batch' when role is set to generate
entries.summary: Batch tokens are lightweight and cannot be renewed, revoked, create children or be root.
internal_causes: Role or auth method uses token_type=batch for a workload that needs renewal or child tokens.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Inspect the token: policies, TTL, entity, namespace
Check the role's token_type
Switch to service tokens or adjust the client

examples:
Code: 400. Errors:

* batch tokens cannot be renewed

entries.title: Lease revocation failing / irrevocable
patterns: lease is expired and has failed previous revocation attempts
failed to revoke an invalid lease
failed to mark lease as irrevocable
entries.summary: Vault keeps failing to revoke leases. The secrets engine cannot delete the credential at the target system.
internal_causes: Secrets engine config broken (root credential rotated outside Vault).
external_causes: Target DB/cloud unreachable or root credentials lack DROP/delete permission.
Target user already deleted manually.

troubleshooting_steps.step: List irrevocable leases
Check the error on irrevocable leases
troubleshooting_steps.command: vault read sys/leases/count; vault read -format=json sys/leases?type=irrevocable

troubleshooting_steps.step: Test the secrets engine connection
After fixing the target, retry revoking the single failed lease
Only if that credential is confirmed gone from the target system, force-revoke that one lease (removes it from Vault without contacting the target)

examples: [ERROR] expiration: failed to revoke lease: lease_id=database/creds/app/abc123 error="failed to revoke entry: resp: (*logical.Response)(nil) err: dial tcp 10.0.2.5:5432: i/o timeout"

entries.title: Error restoring leases on unseal
entries.summary: Loading leases into the expiration manager after unseal/leadership failed or was interrupted.
internal_causes: Very large number of leases (often millions from short-lived tokens) makes leadership changes slow.
external_causes: Storage latency during lease restore.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check lease counts
troubleshooting_steps.command: vault read sys/leases/count -format=json 2>/dev/null || vault read sys/internal/counters/tokens

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check vault.expire.num_leases metric
Reduce lease TTLs / use batch tokens for high-volume logins

examples: [ERROR] expiration: error restoring leases: error="context deadline exceeded"

entries.title: Rate limit / lease count quota exceeded
entries.summary: A resource quota rejected the request (HTTP 429 for rate limits).
internal_causes: Quota too low for the workload.
Retry storm or runaway client creating tokens/leases.

troubleshooting_steps.step: List quotas
troubleshooting_steps.command: vault list sys/quotas/rate-limit; vault list sys/quotas/lease-count

troubleshooting_steps.step: Read the quota that matched
Find the failing request in the audit log
troubleshooting_steps.command: jq -c 'select(.error != null) | {time, type, path: .request.path, error}' /var/log/vault/audit.log | tail -20

examples:
Error making API request.

Code: 429. Errors:

* rate limit quota exceeded

entries.title: Token TTL exceeds allowed maximum
patterns: explicit max TTL of .* is greater than system/mount allowed value
TTL .* is longer than permitted maxTTL
token ttl should not be greater than token max ttl
entries.summary: Requested or configured TTL is above the mount/system max TTL, so Vault caps it.
internal_causes: Role max TTL higher than mount `max_lease_ttl` or system default (32 days).

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check mount tuning
Check the role TTLs
Tune the mount if a longer TTL is intended

examples: [WARN]  Given explicit max TTL of 8760h is greater than system/mount allowed value of 768h seconds

entries.title: Token or lease used across namespaces
patterns: error looking up namespace from the (token|lease)'s namespace ID
entries.summary: A token or lease is used from a namespace different from where it was created.
internal_causes: Client sets VAULT_NAMESPACE (or X-Vault-Namespace) differently for login and renew.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Inspect the token: policies, TTL, entity, namespace
Check the namespace the client sends
Renew/revoke from the namespace that issued the token

examples:
Code: 403. Errors:

* cannot renew a token across namespaces

entries.title: AWS auth role binding mismatch
patterns: IAM Principal .* does not belong to the role
IAM role ARN does not satisfy the constraint on role
account ID does not belong to role
AMI ID does not belong to role
VPC ID does not satisfy the constraint
IAM instance profile ARN does not satisfy the constraint
entries.summary: The AWS identity that logged in does not match the bound_* constraints on the Vault role.
internal_causes: Role bound_iam_principal_arn / bound_account_id / bound_vpc_id wrong.
Principal ARN changed (role recreated) and Vault cached the old unique ID.
external_causes: Workload uses another role (assumed role, IRSA, cross-account) than expected.

troubleshooting_steps.step: From the Vault host, confirm which IAM identity Vault is using
Read the Vault role bindings
Re-save the role to refresh resolved principal IDs

* IAM Principal "arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/app/i-0abc" does not belong to the role "app"

entries.title: AWS auth STS call failed
entries.summary: Vault could not verify the signed sts:GetCallerIdentity request from the client.
internal_causes: iam_server_id_header_value set in Vault but not sent by the client (or the reverse).
STS endpoint/region config mismatch (sts_endpoint, sts_region).
external_causes: Client clock skew breaks the signature.
Vault cannot reach STS (proxy, VPC endpoint).
Expired client credentials.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check Vault's AWS client config
Check client clock
From the Vault host, confirm STS is reachable

examples: Error authenticating: Code: 400. Errors: * error making upstream request: received error code 403 from STS: SignatureDoesNotMatch

entries.title: Kubernetes auth login failed
patterns: lookup failed: service account (unauthorized|jwt not valid)
lookup failed: service account jwt valid for audience
invalid expiration time \(exp\) claim: token is expired
entries.summary: Vault could not validate the pod's service account JWT, or the SA/namespace is not bound to the role.
internal_causes: Role bound_service_account_names / namespaces do not include the pod's SA.
`audience` on the role does not match the projected token audience.
kubernetes_host / CA config wrong.
external_causes: Vault's reviewer token lacks system:auth-delegator (TokenReview forbidden).
SA deleted/recreated, or short-lived token expired.
Vault cannot reach the Kubernetes API.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Read the role bindings
Read the auth config
Check auth-delegator binding for the reviewer SA
troubleshooting_steps.command: kubectl get clusterrolebinding -o wide | grep auth-delegator

troubleshooting_steps.step: Decode the pod JWT to see sa, namespace, aud
troubleshooting_steps.command: kubectl exec <pod> -- cat /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token | cut -d. -f2 | base64 -d 2>/dev/null | jq

examples:
Error authenticating: Code: 403. Errors:

* service account name not authorized

entries.title: LDAP auth bind/search failure
patterns: discovery of user bind DN failed
ldap: (failed to connect|error connecting to host)
entries.summary: Vault could not connect, bind, or find the user/groups in the LDAP directory.
internal_causes: Wrong url, userdn, userattr, groupdn, groupfilter or upndomain.
binddn/bindpass wrong or rotated.
external_causes: Directory unreachable (port 389/636), or TLS CA not trusted.
User locked/disabled (Result Code 49 Invalid Credentials).

troubleshooting_steps.step: Read the auth config
Reproduce the bind from the Vault host
Check TLS to the directory

examples:
Error authenticating: Code: 400. Errors:

* ldap operation failed: failed to bind as user: LDAP Result Code 49 "Invalid Credentials"

entries.title: TLS certificate auth failed
patterns: certificate mismatch of a trusted leaf certificate
invalid certificate or no client certificate supplied
entries.summary: Cert auth did not receive a client certificate, or the cert does not chain to a trusted cert on any role.
internal_causes: CA not registered in auth/cert/certs/<role>, or allowed_* constraints too strict.
external_causes: Load balancer terminates TLS so the client cert never reaches Vault.
Listener tls_disable_client_certs = true.

troubleshooting_steps.step: List trusted cert roles
Test with the client cert directly against a node
Use TCP passthrough on the LB for cert auth

examples:
Error authenticating: Code: 400. Errors:

* client certificate must be supplied

entries.title: AppRole login failed
patterns: bind_secret_id is not set on the role
entries.summary: AppRole rejected the role_id/secret_id pair or the source IP.
internal_causes: secret_id expired, used up (secret_id_num_uses) or from another role.
secret_id_bound_cidrs / token_bound_cidrs exclude the client.
external_causes: Client IP changed (NAT, LB) compared to bound CIDRs.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Look up the secret ID accessor
Read role constraints
Find the failing request in the audit log
troubleshooting_steps.command: jq -c 'select(.error != null) | {time, type, path: .request.path, error}' /var/log/vault/audit.log | tail -20

examples:
Error writing data to auth/approle/login: Code: 400. Errors:

* invalid role or secret ID

entries.title: Invalid username or password
entries.summary: Userpass (or similar) login rejected the credentials.
internal_causes: Wrong password, wrong mount path, or user missing.
User lockout after repeated failures.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check the user exists on the mount
Check user lockout
Find the failing request in the audit log
troubleshooting_steps.command: jq -c 'select(.error != null) | {time, type, path: .request.path, error}' /var/log/vault/audit.log | tail -20

examples:
Error authenticating: Code: 400. Errors:

* invalid username or password

entries.title: PKI role does not allow the requested name
patterns: (common name|subject alternate name|email address|other SAN OID|serial_number) .* not allowed by this role
IP Subject Alternative Names are not allowed in this role
role \(.*\) will not issue certificate for name
entries.summary: The PKI role's allowed_domains / allow_* flags do not permit the requested CN or SANs.
internal_causes: allowed_domains missing the domain, or allow_subdomains / allow_glob_domains / allow_bare_domains not set.
allow_ip_sans false.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Read the role
Update only the role constraints you need (patch keeps the other role settings; `vault write` would reset them)

examples:
Error writing data to pki/issue/web: Code: 400. Errors:

* common name app.internal.example.org not allowed by this role

entries.title: PKI issuer missing or unusable
patterns: issuer missing proper issuance usage or key
unable to fetch corresponding key for issuer
could not fetch the CA certificate \(was one set\?\)
entries.summary: The PKI mount has no usable issuer (none generated/imported, default not set, or key missing).
internal_causes: Mount never got a root/intermediate.
Default issuer deleted, or issuer has leaf_not_after_behavior/usage limits.
external_causes: Managed key (HSM/KMS) for the issuer unavailable (Enterprise).

troubleshooting_steps.step: List issuers
Check the default issuer
Set the default

examples:
Code: 500. Errors:

* no default issuer currently configured

entries.title: Certificate TTL beyond CA expiration
patterns: beyond the expiration of the CA certificate
entries.summary: The requested cert would outlive the issuing CA, and leaf_not_after_behavior is `err`.
internal_causes: Intermediate CA near expiry.
Requested TTL too long.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check CA expiry
Rotate the intermediate, lower the TTL, or set leaf_not_after_behavior=truncate

examples:
Code: 400. Errors:

* cannot satisfy request, as TTL would result in notAfter of 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z that is beyond the expiration of the CA certificate at 2025-06-01T00:00:00Z

entries.title: PKI CRL build failure
patterns: CRL was not updated, as it exceeds the configured max size
entries.summary: Vault could not build or update the CRL for one or more issuers.
internal_causes: Very many revoked, unexpired certificates (no tidy).
Imported issuer needs revocation_signature_algorithm (PSS-only managed keys).
external_causes: Managed key/HSM unavailable for signing.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Run tidy to drop expired revoked certs
Check CRL config
Force a rebuild

examples: [ERROR] secrets.pki: CRL was not updated, as it exceeds the configured max size.  The CRL now does not contain all revoked certificates!

entries.title: PKI issuer migration not complete
patterns: Can not .* until migration has completed
entries.summary: After an upgrade the PKI mount is still migrating legacy CA storage to the multi-issuer layout.
internal_causes: Upgrade in progress; on replicated clusters the primary must finish first.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Wait and retry; check the server log for PKI migration messages
Check seal, HA and storage state of this node

examples:
Code: 500. Errors:

* Can not get issuer until migration has completed

entries.title: Transit key not found
entries.summary: The named transit key does not exist on this mount/namespace.
internal_causes: Wrong key name, mount path or namespace.
Key deleted (deletion_allowed).

troubleshooting_steps.step: List keys
Read the key

examples:
Code: 400. Errors:

* encryption key not found

entries.title: Transit key version too old
patterns: version is too old \(disallowed by policy\)
invalid ciphertext: version is too new
entries.summary: The ciphertext uses a key version below min_decryption_version (or above the latest).
internal_causes: min_decryption_version raised after rotation without rewrapping data.
Ciphertext from another cluster/key.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check key versions
Rewrap data to the latest version
Lower min_decryption_version if needed

examples:
Code: 400. Errors:

* cannot use key version 1: version is too old (disallowed by policy) for key app

entries.title: Invalid transit ciphertext
patterns: invalid ciphertext: (no prefix|wrong number of fields|could not decode base64|version number could not be decoded)
entries.summary: The ciphertext is malformed, truncated, or was encrypted with another key/context.
internal_causes: App stores only part of the vault:vN:... string.
Derived key decrypted without the same context.
Wrong key name.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check the ciphertext starts with vault:v<N>:
Make sure context/nonce match the encrypt call
Confirm the key name used for encrypt

examples:
Code: 400. Errors:

* invalid ciphertext: no prefix

entries.title: Audit device failed / not accessible
patterns: audit device not accessible at startup
file sink creation failed for path
failed to close file audit backend
entries.summary: An audit device could not write. If every enabled device fails, Vault blocks requests so it never serves an unaudited request.
internal_causes: Audit path changed in config/API without creating the directory.
external_causes: Disk full or volume read-only.
File owned by another user (logrotate created it as root).
Socket target down / syslog daemon not running.

troubleshooting_steps.step: List devices and options
Check disk and permissions
Check logrotate uses copytruncate or sends SIGHUP to Vault
Enable a second device so one failure does not block Vault

examples: [ERROR] audit: backend failed to log request: backend=file/ error="file sink creation failed for path \"/var/log/vault/audit.log\": open /var/log/vault/audit.log: permission denied"

Code: 500. Errors:

* audit system internal error

entries.title: Audit file path not allowed
patterns: audit file target may not be in the plugin directory
error resolving audit file path for audit validation
audit prefix may not contain control characters
entries.summary: Vault rejected the audit device options during enable.
internal_causes: file_path inside plugin_directory, or invalid prefix.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Choose a dedicated audit directory outside plugin_directory

examples:
Code: 400. Errors:

* audit file target may not be in the plugin directory

entries.title: Entity on token disabled or invalid
patterns: permission denied as the entity on the token is (invalid|disabled)
entries.summary: The token is tied to an identity entity that is disabled or no longer exists.
internal_causes: Operator set disabled=true on the entity.
Entity deleted/merged while tokens were still valid.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Inspect the token: policies, TTL, entity, namespace
Read the entity
Re-enable it, or log in again to get a token for the current entity

examples:
Code: 403. Errors:

* permission denied as the entity on the token is disabled

entries.title: Identity alias conflict
patterns: alias with combination of mount accessor and name already exists
alias already exists for requested entity and mount accessor
alias cannot be updated as the (given )?entity already has an alias
Entity has multiple aliases on the same mount
entries.summary: An entity alias for this mount accessor and name already exists, or an entity would get two aliases on one mount.
internal_causes: Automation creating aliases twice.
Merging entities that both have aliases on the same mount.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Look up the alias by name and mount accessor
Merge entities and pick the alias to keep
troubleshooting_steps.command: vault write identity/entity/merge from_entity_ids=<id> to_entity_id=<id> conflicting_alias_ids_to_keep=<alias_id>

examples:
Code: 400. Errors:

* alias with combination of mount accessor and name already exists

entries.title: Identity duplicates detected
entries.summary: On unseal Vault found duplicate entities, aliases or groups (often only case differences) from older versions.
internal_causes: Historical bugs or case-insensitive identity created duplicates.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Collect the following log lines that list duplicates
Follow the deduplication guide before upgrading or enabling strict mode

examples: [WARN]  identity: DUPLICATES DETECTED, see following logs for details and refer to https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/upgrading/identity-deduplication for resolution.

entries.title: Encryption keys changed (replication enabled)
patterns: encryption keys have changed out from underneath us
entries.summary: Enabling replication as a secondary replaced this cluster's keyring with the primary's, so the node must be unsealed again.
internal_causes: Secondary activation, or a node lagging after activation.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check seal, HA and storage state of this node
Unseal with the primary's unseal/recovery keys (auto-unseal will retry)
Check replication status

examples: [ERROR] core: encryption keys have changed out from underneath us (possibly due to replication enabling), must be unsealed again

entries.title: Operation only allowed on primary
patterns: rekeying can only be performed on the primary cluster
cannot rotate on a replication secondary
token hmac key has not been initialized or has not been replicated yet
entries.summary: The operation must run on the primary, or replicated state has not arrived yet.
internal_causes: Running rekey/rotate on a secondary.
Secondary still bootstrapping after activation.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check replication mode
Run the operation on the primary cluster
Stream server logs at debug level without a restart

examples:
Code: 400. Errors:

* rekeying can only be performed on the primary cluster when replication is activated

entries.title: Replication connectivity / state errors
patterns: replication.*(connection refused|i/o timeout|context deadline exceeded|transport: Error while dialing|connection error)
entries.summary: Replication traffic between clusters (cluster port 8201, gRPC) fails, or replication state is not yet known.
internal_causes: primary_cluster_addr wrong or points at a load balancer that is not TCP passthrough.
Secondary activation token expired.
external_causes: Firewall between data centers blocks 8201.
TLS-inspecting middlebox on 8201.

troubleshooting_steps.step: Check status on both clusters
Check the primary cluster address the secondary uses
Test the cluster port from the secondary
Stream server logs at debug level without a restart

examples: [ERROR] replication: error="rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = \"transport: Error while dialing dial tcp 10.1.0.11:8201: i/o timeout\""

source.note: Vault Enterprise replication (gRPC over the cluster port)
